title: UID normalization heuristic scratch notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for normalizing 'IDs' in text during labeling and cleanup. Focus is on making a small, conservative normalization that preserves linkability for downstream dedupe / QA while minimizing over-normalization that hides semantics (e.g., SKU vs invoice vs phone).

Context / motivation:
- We get lots of noisy tokens that look like identifiers but vary wildly (leading zeros, separators, mixed-case prefixes). Annotators are inconsistent (some strip hyphens, others keep them).
- Model training / evaluation requires a canonical representation so metrics and downstream joins are stable.
- We also must balance privacy: some datasets require pseudonymization for real PII ids, others need stable hashing-friendly canonicalization.

High-level goals (practical):
1) Detect and tag UID-like tokens with reasonable precision (minimize false positives).
2) Canonicalize to a compact, reversible-ish form for internal workflows: preserve checksum/namespace if present, collapse cosmetic separators, normalize homoglyphs.
3) Flag ambiguous tokens for adjudication rather than auto-normalize.
4) Produce an audit trail: original -> normalized mapping stored with examples.

Definitions / scope (working):
- UID-like token: short-to-medium length token (4-30 chars) that is primarily alphanumeric and used as a reference (user id, order id, invoice, transaction, session).
- Exclusions: phone numbers, credit-card-looking sequences (16-digit contiguous numeric), bank routing numbers (where regulated). For now, phone/cc detection uses separate pipeline.

Examples and rules (prioritized):
1) Trim surrounding noise: strip surrounding punctuation like parentheses, quotes, trailing colons when token boundary clear. E.g. "(ord-0001234)" -> "ord-0001234".
2) Collapse common separators to single hyphen between alpha/numeric groups: spaces, slashes, dots, underscores -> hyphen. "USR 0001" -> "USR-0001"; "a.b_c/123" -> "a-b-c-123".
3) Normalize prefix case: preserve original if prefix is all-caps acronym (ORD, INV, TXN) -> uppercase prefixes; otherwise lowercase whole token if no strong domain cue. Rule: if token starts with 2–5 letters followed by separator then digits, canonicalize prefix uppercase (helps grouping).
4) Leading zeros: do NOT drop leading zeros for tokens with explicit prefixes (ORD-00023 remains ORD-00023). For bare numeric tokens where context suggests serial number and we need numeric identity, canonicalize to minimal numeric + marker: e.g., "00023" -> "#23" only if annotator confirms numeric-serial. Otherwise keep as-is.
5) Remove visual homoglyph noise: map fullwidth digits/letters to ASCII, map zero-like O/Ø to 0 only when token is majority numeric; otherwise keep letter O. Keep a confidence flag if mapping applied.
6) Checksum / modulus endings: if token matches known pattern (e.g., 12-digit + 1 check digit), keep check digit and mark pattern type (MD5-like not detected here).
7) Preserve namespace separators: if token uses two-part namespace (e.g., acct:12345, proj#A-12), canonicalize to lowercase namespace + colon + body -> "acct:12345".
8) Limit length: if token > 40 chars and looks hashed (base64-like or hex with high entropy), mark as "HASH-LIKE" and DO NOT attempt more normalization.

Ambiguous decisions / heuristics to adjudicate (examples):
- "ID: 0012" vs "User 0012": when a labeler sees the word "User" treat as username-like; if purely "ID:" leave prefix but suggest mapping rules.
- "AB12-34CD": could be SKU, product code, or composite. Heuristic: if token appears frequently in product catalogs -> SKU; else tag as GENERIC-ALPHANUM.
- "O12345" vs "012345": visual zero vs letter O. Heuristic: if many tokens of same family have numeric-only forms, prefer 0; else flag.

Annotator UI guidance (short checklist):
- If you can look up the token in a system or dataset and confirm semantics, choose the semantic type (ORDER/USER/SKU).
- If token looks like a phone or cc, stop and use phone/cc tool.
- Do NOT strip leading zeros unless instructed.
- If token is long, contains non-ASCII, or base64-like chars (+, /), mark HASH-LIKE and add comment why.
- Use the "flag for review" button when unsure (we almost always prefer a human instead of wrong auto-normalization).

Canonical form examples (recommended):
- Original: "usr_000123" -> Canonical: "USR-000123" (preserve prefix upper, separators->hyphen)
- Original: " order/12.003 " -> Canonical: "ORD-12-003" (strip outer whitespace, map separators)
- Original: "inv#AB-21-zz" -> Canonical: "INV-AB-21-ZZ" (prefix upper, body uppercase for alpha segments)
- Original: "00004567" -> Canonical: "00004567" (leave as-is unless numeric-serial signal)
- Original: "Ǥ123" (unicode G-variant) -> Canonical: "G-123"

Mini-regex bank (illustrative, annotators not required to write these):
- Namespace prefix: ^([A-Za-z]{2,5})[\s._:/#-]+([A-Za-z0-9\-]+)$
- Bare numeric: ^0*[0-9]{2,10}$
- Hash-like (hex): ^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$
- High-entropy/base64: [+/=] present AND length>24 -> mark as HASH-LIKE

Normalization pseudocode (conceptual):
- function normalize(token):
    raw = trim(token)
    if matches HASH-LIKE -> return {kind: "HASH-LIKE", norm: raw, note: "no-normalize"}
    raw = map_fullwidth_and_homoglyphs(raw) -> (mapped, hint)
    parts = split_on_separators(mapped)
    if looks_like(namespace) -> prefix = normalize_prefix(parts[0]); body = join(parts[1:]); body = collapse_internal_separators(body); return prefix + '-' + body
    if looks_numeric_serial(raw) -> maybe_numeric = true -> keep leading zeros unless numeric-only-canonicalize flag
    return cleaned

Audit / QA plan:
- Keep table of (original, normalized, rule_applied, annotator, date). Store as CSV export from labeling UI for audits.
- Sample 1k normalized tokens weekly, compute false-normalization rate (human review) goal < 2%.
- Track most common normalization rules applied (top 10) and their error rates.

Operational notes / integration:
- Hook normalization as a pre-labeling pipeline step visible to annotator, with "view original" toggle.
- Normalizer should provide confidence score and rule id for traceability.
- For datasets requiring pseudonymization, normalized form is the input to deterministic hash(salt) -> pseudonym (store mapping in secure store).

Open questions / TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Finalize list of prefixes that should be forced uppercase (ORD, INV, TXN, USR, ACCT) — ask product for canonical list.
- [ ] Define rule for when to shorten long numeric strings (bank refs) vs mark as SENSITIVE. Legal needs to weigh in.
- [ ] Decide default for leading-zero numeric tokens: keep by default, but pipeline flag to minimize (discuss with analytics for joins).
- [ ] Add small adjudication UX: show candidate normalizations and let annotator accept/modify.
- [ ] Create small eval harness - feed 2k sample tokens into current normalizer and measure disagreements with 3 annotators. Ticket: PROJ-3421.

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep normalization conservative. We can always add downstream merging heuristics (fuzzy match) if needed.
- Preserve original in metadata! So any mistake can be rolled back.

Stray examples to test when implementing (copy into unit tests):
- "usr:O0l-000" (letter O vs zero vs letter l)
- "acct/000-999"
- "aBc-12_34"
- "000012345678901234567890" (long numeric)
- "dGVzdF9oYXNoLXRlc3Q=" (base64)
- "INV-4321-9" (possible check digit)

References / links for follow-up:
- ticket PROJ-3421 (normalizer prototyping)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/modeltools/pull/512 (initial normalizer impl)

End of scratch notes.

-- Evelyn
